newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany evacuates thousands as flood bursts dyke.
newsitem.headline: Germany evacuates thousands as flood bursts dyke.

text.p: German rescuers raced on Wednesday to evacuate areas along the swollen Oder river as floods which have already wreaked havoc in neighbouring Poland and the Czech Republic poured into Germany.

Thousands of border guards, soldiers, local police and volunteers worked around the clock with 36 airforce helicopters to shore up the banks of the Oder after one dyke reinforcing its banks burst and others threatened to collapse.

As evacuations gathered pace in Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic struggled to deal with the aftermath of floods in both countries earlier this month, which have claimed more than one hundred lives.

The Czech Republic prepared to observe one minute of silence at noon (1000 GMT) on Thursday in honour of its 48 flood victims and most Polish political parties demanded a delay to a September 21 general election because of the floods.

The Polish opposition parties said the president should declare a state of emergency in flood-hit areas which would automatically postpone the polls and enable the country to focus on repairing the damage caused by the floods.

The flooding, which began with torrential rains earlier this month, has begun to subside in the Czech Republic and Poland, but thousands of homes have been destroyed, communications ruined, crops swamped and livestock drowned.
Flood alerts were still in force on some Czech rivers but better weather was forecast after days of torrential rain.

In Germany, emergency workers began evacuating around 5,000 inhabitants in areas south of Frankfurt an der Oder and at the confluence of the Oder and Neisse rivers as around 500 cubic metres of water poured every second through a hole in a dyke.
Brandenburg state environment minister Matthias Platzeck said the flooding could reach a depth of seven metres, but said the nearby town of Eisenhuettenstadt was not in danger.
Officials said water levels could rise by 30 cm (10 inches) overnight and that dykes were so porous that large swathes of the area could be under water by early next week.
They said a new high-water swell was advancing down the Oder, which forms part of the German-Polish border, and said the wave would reach the affected part of Germany in the early hours of Thursday.

"The flooding is by no means over," Alwin Ziel, interior minister of the state of Brandenburg, said in a radio interview. "There will be another wave. Those who are not able to join emergency teams must get out."
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann reiterated a pledge by Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who visited the area on Tuesday, to help in every way possible.
Hausmann said the cabinet had discussed the crisis in the morning and decided to earmark a 200 million mark ($110 million) reconstruction fund for the area once the catastrophe was over.
Interior Minister Manfred Kanther and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe were both due to visit the region on Thursday.
